items.q: A gas has a specific heat at constant pressure of 1.005 kJ/kg K and a gas constant of 296 J/kg K. Calculate its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.
Calculate the heat needed, in kJ, to raise 12 kg of a substance of specific heat capacity 4.18 kJ/kg K through 30 K.
An engine receives 800 kJ of heat and delivers 250 kJ of work. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
The universal gas constant is 8314 J/kmol K. Find the gas constant, in J/kg K, of a gas whose molar mass is 4 kg/kmol.
A mass of 3 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 260 J/kg K occupies 1.5 m3 at a pressure of 300 kPa. Calculate its temperature in K.
Air of gas constant 287 J/kg K is at a pressure of 100 kPa and a temperature of 300 K. Calculate its density in kg/m3.
A gas has specific heats of 1.04 kJ/kg K at constant pressure and 0.85 kJ/kg K at constant volume. Calculate the ratio of specific heats.
A gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.1 kJ/kg K has a ratio of specific heats of 1.41. Find its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.
items.s: cv = cp/gamma = 1.1/1.41 = 0.7801 kJ/kg K.

items.q: A rigid vessel of volume 3.0 m3 contains steam of specific volume 0.4 m3/kg. Calculate the mass of steam in the vessel in kg.
A quantity of 300 kJ of heat raises the temperature of a body of specific heat capacity 0.718 kJ/kg K by 25 K. Find its mass in kg.
Calculate the heat required, in kJ, to change 2.5 kg of a substance completely from liquid to vapour at its boiling point, given a latent heat of 198 kJ/kg.
A gas expands at a constant pressure of 150 kPa from 0.2 m3 to 3.0 m3. Calculate the work done in kJ.
3 kg of gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.04 kJ/kg K is heated through 40 K at constant pressure. Find the heat supplied in kJ.
4 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 296 J/kg K expands isothermally at 350 K until its volume is 6 times the original. Calculate the work done in kJ.
items.s: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) = 4 x 296 x 350 x ln 6 = 742.5 kJ.

items.q: A gas is compressed polytropically from 250 kPa and 2.0 m3 to 600 kPa and 0.3 m3, with an index of compression of 1.3. Calculate the work input in kJ.
2 kg of air of specific heat at constant volume 0.8 kJ/kg K expands adiabatically from 600 K to 350 K. Calculate the work done in kJ.
Find the change in internal energy, in kJ, of 5 kg of gas of specific heat at constant volume 0.75 kJ/kg K when its temperature rises by 60 K.
items.s: dU = m cv dT = 5 x 0.75 x 60 = 225 kJ.

items.q: During a process a closed system absorbs heat while its internal energy rises by 80 kJ and it does 25 kJ of work. Calculate the heat absorbed in kJ.
Calculate the change in enthalpy, in kJ, of 6 kg of gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.1 kJ/kg K when it is heated through 30 K.
items.s: dH = m cp dT = 6 x 1.1 x 30 = 198 kJ.

A mass of 4 kg of gas with gas constant 519 J/kg K is held at 150 kPa and 350 K. Find its volume in m3.
A gas at 320 K is compressed adiabatically through a volume ratio of 6 : 1. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.3, find the final temperature in K.
A gas at 100 kPa is compressed adiabatically to one 6th of its original volume. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.4, calculate the final pressure in kPa.

A boiler raises 1.5 kg/s of water from an enthalpy of 500 kJ/kg to steam of enthalpy 2800 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat added in kW.
A boiler evaporates 2.5 kg/s of water with an enthalpy rise of 2400 kJ/kg while burning 0.18 kg/s of fuel of calorific value 43000 kJ/kg. Calculate the boiler efficiency in percent.
A reversible engine works between a source at 600 K and a sink at 280 K. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
A Carnot engine receives 500 kJ of heat from a reservoir at 500 K and rejects heat to a sink at 320 K. Calculate the work output in kJ.
A heat engine takes in 1500 kJ of heat and produces 300 kJ of work. Find the heat rejected to the sink in kJ.

A heat pump delivers 1200 kJ of heat to a room for 200 kJ of work input. Calculate its coefficient of performance.
1 kg of gas of cp = 1.1 kJ/kg K and R = 260 J/kg K is changed from 300 K and 400 kPa to 550 K and 100 kPa. Find the entropy change in kJ/K.
An air standard Otto cycle operates with a compression ratio of 9 : 1 and gamma = 1.4. Calculate its air standard efficiency in percent.
An air standard Diesel cycle has a compression ratio of 18 : 1 and a cut off ratio of 1.8, with gamma = 1.35. Calculate its air standard efficiency in percent.
items.s: eta = 1 - (1/r^(gamma-1))[(rc^gamma - 1)/(gamma(rc - 1))] with r = 18, rc = 1.8, gamma = 1.35 = 59.22%.

A gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.1 kJ/kg K has a ratio of specific heats of 1.35. Find its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.

a change carried out at constant temperature
energy crossing a boundary because of a difference in temperature
a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition

items.q: The statement “vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure” describes which of the following?

Saturation temperature
Saturation pressure
Superheated vapour

items.q: Which term is described by “a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from”?

Open system
Cycle
Boundary
items.s: Cycle is a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from.

items.q: Ideal gas may be defined as
o: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
items.s: Ideal gas: a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another. The other options describe Cut off ratio, Absolute pressure, Equation of state.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall”?
o: Entropy
T-s diagram
Principle of increase of entropy
Available energy
items.s: Principle of increase of entropy is the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Thermal efficiency?
o: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
items.s: Thermal efficiency: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work. The other options describe Process, Carnot efficiency, Displacement work.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Compression ratio?
o: the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume
the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
the delivery pressure of a compressor divided by the pressure at its inlet
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
items.s: Compression ratio: the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume. The other options describe Heat engine, Pressure ratio, Temperature.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Universal gas constant?
o: the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
the mass of vapour in a mixture expressed as a fraction of the total mass of the mixture
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
items.s: Universal gas constant: the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state. The other options describe Dryness fraction, Process, Critical point.

items.q: Ratio of specific heats may be defined as
o: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
the energy needed to raise unit mass of a substance through one degree
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
items.s: Ratio of specific heats: the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air. The other options describe Carnot efficiency, Specific heat capacity, Thermal reservoir.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Superheated vapour.
o: a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
the pressure at which a liquid boils at a given temperature
vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure
the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall
items.s: Superheated vapour: vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure. The other options describe Adiabatic wall, Saturation pressure, Principle of increase of entropy.

items.q: Which term is described by “a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant”?
o: Equation of state
Adiabatic process
Polytropic process
Gas constant

items.q: Carnot efficiency may be defined as
o: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the mass of vapour in a mixture expressed as a fraction of the total mass of the mixture
the principle that heat cannot pass from a colder body to a hotter one without work being spent
items.s: Carnot efficiency: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures. The other options describe Dryness fraction, Second law of thermodynamics, Intensive property.

items.q: Reversible process may be defined as
o: the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them
the plot of temperature against disorder on which the heat of a reversible process is the area beneath
an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
items.s: Reversible process: an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings. The other options describe T-s diagram, Ratio of specific heats, Thermodynamics.

items.q: The statement “the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point” describes which of the following?
o: Sensible enthalpy of liquid
Critical point
Pure substance
Superheated vapour
items.s: Sensible enthalpy of liquid is the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point.

items.q: Which term is described by “the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region”?
o: Flow work
Nozzle
Steady flow
Diffuser
items.s: Flow work is the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Molar mass?
o: the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
matter of fixed chemical composition that may exist in more than one phase
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
the mass of one kilomole of a substance
items.s: Molar mass: the mass of one kilomole of a substance. The other options describe Cut off ratio, Temperature, Pure substance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Adiabatic process?
o: a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
the constant specific to a particular gas in the equation of state, equal to the universal value divided by molar mass
the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area
the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
items.s: Adiabatic process: a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary. The other options describe Coefficient of performance, Indicator diagram, Gas constant.

items.q: The statement “energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature” describes which of the following?
o: Displacement work
Heat
Diathermic wall
Latent heat
items.s: Latent heat is energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Entropy?
o: the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work
everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it
items.s: Entropy: the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work. The other options describe Available energy, Irreversibility, Surroundings.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Wet vapour?
o: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition
the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall
a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
items.s: Wet vapour: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition. The other options describe Throttling, Principle of increase of entropy, Diathermic wall.

items.q: Wet vapour may be defined as
o: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
the mass of one kilomole of a substance
items.s: Wet vapour: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition. The other options describe Specific heat at constant volume, Molar mass, Adiabatic process.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Available energy?
o: a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions
a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work
items.s: Available energy: the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work. The other options describe Entropy, Extensive property, Quasi static process.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Cycle.
o: the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
items.s: Cycle: a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from. The other options describe Critical point, Diathermic wall, Process.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Thermal reservoir?
o: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
items.s: Thermal reservoir: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature. The other options describe Compression ratio, Critical point, Adiabatic wall.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Quasi static process?
o: the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
items.s: Quasi static process: a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions. The other options describe Cut off ratio, Saturation temperature, Universal gas constant.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Triple point?
o: a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance
a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition
items.s: Triple point: the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance. The other options describe Throttling, Property, Adiabatic wall.

items.q: Nozzle may be defined as
o: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level
energy crossing a boundary because of a difference in temperature
a duct of decreasing area in which a fluid gains velocity at the expense of pressure
items.s: Nozzle: a duct of decreasing area in which a fluid gains velocity at the expense of pressure. The other options describe Heat, Equation of state, Gauge pressure.

items.q: Absolute pressure may be defined as
o: the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance
an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas
items.s: Absolute pressure: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero. The other options describe Sensible heat, Air standard cycle, Critical point.

items.q: Which term is described by “energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance”?
o: Latent heat
Adiabatic wall
Heat
Sensible heat
items.s: Sensible heat is energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance.

items.q: Adiabatic process may be defined as
o: energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it
the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
items.s: Adiabatic process: a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary. The other options describe Latent heat, Pressure, Otto cycle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point”?
o: Enthalpy of vaporisation
Sensible enthalpy of liquid
Superheated vapour
Wet vapour
items.s: Sensible enthalpy of liquid is the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Diathermic wall?
o: the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
items.s: Diathermic wall: a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise. The other options describe Entropy, Absolute pressure, Process.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Carnot efficiency?
o: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
items.s: Carnot efficiency: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures. The other options describe Polytropic process, Critical point, Diesel cycle.

items.q: The statement “an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas” describes which of the following?
o: Otto cycle
Diesel cycle
Dual cycle
Air standard cycle
items.s: Air standard cycle is an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas.

items.q: Dual cycle may be defined as
o: a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure
the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process
items.s: Dual cycle: the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure. The other options describe First law of thermodynamics, Cut off ratio, Intensive property.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Diathermic wall?
o: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
items.s: Diathermic wall: a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise. The other options describe Thermal efficiency, Ideal gas, Specific heat at constant volume.

items.q: Specific volume may be defined as
o: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance
the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
items.s: Specific volume: the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance. The other options describe Otto cycle, Equation of state, Ideal gas.

items.q: The statement “energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance” describes which of the following?
o: Displacement work
Latent heat
Work
Specific heat capacity
items.s: Work is energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance.

items.q: Internal energy may be defined as
o: the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules
energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance
items.s: Internal energy: the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules. The other options describe Thermal reservoir, Coefficient of performance, Work.

items.q: Which term is described by “a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added”?
o: Throttling
Enthalpy
Steady flow
Diffuser

the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour
a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Isolated system?
o: a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from
a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Sensible heat?
o: the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour
a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance
items.s: Sensible heat: energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance. The other options describe Enthalpy of vaporisation, Diffuser, Thermal reservoir.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Intensive property?
o: the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
items.s: Intensive property: a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Thermal efficiency, Triple point.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Throttling?
o: a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
items.s: Throttling: a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added. The other options describe Saturation temperature, Specific heat at constant volume, Ratio of specific heats.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Wet vapour?
o: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings
items.s: Wet vapour: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition. The other options describe Specific heat at constant volume, Enthalpy, Ideal gas.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Entropy?
o: an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point
items.s: Entropy: the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work. The other options describe Process, Reversible process, Sensible enthalpy of liquid.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Boundary?
o: the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
the plot of temperature against disorder on which the heat of a reversible process is the area beneath
the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings
the closed surface that separates the matter under study from everything around it

the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
items.s: Equation of state: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas. The other options describe Isothermal process, Adiabatic process, Specific heat at constant volume.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Control volume.
o: the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process
the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance
a duct of decreasing area in which a fluid gains velocity at the expense of pressure
the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules
items.s: Control volume: the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance. The other options describe First law of thermodynamics, Internal energy, Nozzle.

items.q: Dryness fraction is best described as
o: the mass of vapour in a mixture expressed as a fraction of the total mass of the mixture
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
matter of fixed chemical composition that may exist in more than one phase
the pressure at which a liquid boils at a given temperature
items.s: Dryness fraction: the mass of vapour in a mixture expressed as a fraction of the total mass of the mixture. The other options describe Saturation pressure, Critical point, Pure substance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Brayton cycle.
o: the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
the ideal cycle of a gas turbine, with compression and expansion in steady flow
items.s: Brayton cycle: the ideal cycle of a gas turbine, with compression and expansion in steady flow. The other options describe Diesel cycle, Otto cycle, Dual cycle.

items.q: Thermal efficiency may be defined as
o: an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
items.s: Thermal efficiency: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work. The other options describe Carnot efficiency, Reversible process, Thermal reservoir.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Dual cycle?
o: an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume
the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure
items.s: Dual cycle: the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure. The other options describe Compression ratio, Air standard cycle, Diesel cycle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour”?
o: Enthalpy of vaporisation
Wet vapour
Triple point
Saturation temperature
items.s: Enthalpy of vaporisation is the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour.

items.q: Which term is described by “an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas”?
o: Otto cycle
Dual cycle
Cut off ratio
Air standard cycle
items.s: Air standard cycle is an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Work and heat?
o: Heat
Work
Displacement work
Property
items.s: Every other option belongs to Work and heat. “Property” belongs to Basic concepts, not Work and heat.

items.q: Thermal efficiency is best described as
o: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
items.s: Thermal efficiency: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work. The other options describe Carnot efficiency, Thermal reservoir, Coefficient of performance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Specific volume.
o: a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance
the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
items.s: Specific volume: the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance. The other options describe Extensive property, Intensive property, Pressure.

items.q: Which term is described by “an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings”?
o: Reversible process
Thermal reservoir
Irreversibility
Coefficient of performance
items.s: Reversible process is an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Surroundings?
o: a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it
a region through which both mass and energy may flow
the complete set of property values that fixes the condition of a working substance
items.s: Surroundings: everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it. The other options describe Open system, State, Isolated system.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Polytropic process?
o: the constant specific to a particular gas in the equation of state, equal to the universal value divided by molar mass
a change carried out at constant temperature
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
items.s: Polytropic process: a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant. The other options describe Isothermal process, Universal gas constant, Gas constant.

items.q: Which term is described by “the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work”?
o: Available energy
T-s diagram
Entropy generation
Entropy
items.s: Entropy is the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Displacement work?
o: the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance
energy crossing a boundary because of a difference in temperature
items.s: Displacement work: the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary. The other options describe Work, Heat, Diathermic wall.

items.q: Which term is described by “a change carried out at constant temperature”?
o: Isothermal process
Polytropic process
Equation of state
Molar mass
items.s: Isothermal process is a change carried out at constant temperature.

items.q: Specific heat capacity is best described as
o: the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area
energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
the energy needed to raise unit mass of a substance through one degree
items.s: Specific heat capacity: the energy needed to raise unit mass of a substance through one degree. The other options describe Sensible heat, Indicator diagram, Displacement work.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Thermal reservoir.
o: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
items.s: Thermal reservoir: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature. The other options describe Irreversibility, Reversible process, Thermal efficiency.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Thermodynamics.
o: a region of fixed mass across whose edge only energy may pass
a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from
the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them
the closed surface that separates the matter under study from everything around it
items.s: Thermodynamics: the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them. The other options describe Closed system, Boundary, Cycle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Ratio of specific heats?
o: a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
items.s: Ratio of specific heats: the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Polytropic process, Adiabatic process.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Specific heat at constant volume?
o: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
items.s: Specific heat at constant volume: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed. The other options describe Polytropic process, Ratio of specific heats, Ideal gas.

items.q: Temperature is best described as
o: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
the mass of a substance contained in unit volume
a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
items.s: Temperature: the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow. The other options describe Density, Absolute pressure, Extensive property.

items.q: Which term is described by “the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone”?
o: Heat engine
Carnot efficiency
Second law of thermodynamics
Irreversibility
items.s: Irreversibility is the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone.

items.q: Entropy may be defined as
o: an ideal change during which the disorder of the substance stays constant
the disorder produced inside a real device by friction, unrestrained expansion and mixing
the plot of temperature against disorder on which the heat of a reversible process is the area beneath
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
items.s: Entropy: the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work. The other options describe T-s diagram, Entropy generation, Isentropic process.

items.q: Heat engine is best described as
o: the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
items.s: Heat engine: a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest. The other options describe Coefficient of performance, Reversible process, Carnot efficiency.

items.q: Saturation temperature is best described as
o: the pressure at which a liquid boils at a given temperature
the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure
the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
items.s: Saturation temperature: the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure. The other options describe Critical point, Enthalpy of vaporisation, Saturation pressure.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Heat engine.
o: the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
items.s: Heat engine: a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest. The other options describe Thermal reservoir, Reversible process, Thermal efficiency.

items.q: Which term is described by “a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions”?
o: Quasi static process
Process
Thermodynamics
Cycle
items.s: Quasi static process is a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Carnot efficiency.
o: an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
items.s: Carnot efficiency: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures. The other options describe Thermal reservoir, Thermal efficiency, Reversible process.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Absolute pressure?
o: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level
items.s: Absolute pressure: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero. The other options describe Extensive property, Gauge pressure, Temperature.

items.q: Diathermic wall may be defined as
o: energy crossing a boundary because of a difference in temperature
a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
items.s: Diathermic wall: a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise. The other options describe Adiabatic wall, Displacement work, Heat.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mass of one kilomole of a substance”?
o: Molar mass
Equation of state
Ideal gas
Isothermal process
items.s: Molar mass is the mass of one kilomole of a substance.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other”?
o: Critical point
Triple point
Saturation temperature
Wet vapour
items.s: Critical point is the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Adiabatic process?
o: the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
the constant specific to a particular gas in the equation of state, equal to the universal value divided by molar mass
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the pressure is held fixed
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
items.s: Adiabatic process: a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary. The other options describe Gas constant, Ratio of specific heats, Specific heat at constant pressure.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Isothermal process.
o: a change carried out at constant temperature
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
the mass of one kilomole of a substance
items.s: Isothermal process: a change carried out at constant temperature. The other options describe Molar mass, Ideal gas, Specific heat at constant volume.

items.q: Which term is described by “the scale that begins at absolute zero and is measured in kelvin”?
o: Thermodynamic temperature scale
Extensive property
Density
Temperature
items.s: Thermodynamic temperature scale is the scale that begins at absolute zero and is measured in kelvin.

items.q: Surroundings is best described as
o: a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it
the complete set of property values that fixes the condition of a working substance
the closed surface that separates the matter under study from everything around it
items.s: Surroundings: everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it. The other options describe Isolated system, State, Boundary.

items.q: Which term is described by “the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area”?
o: Displacement work
Indicator diagram
Work
Heat
items.s: Indicator diagram is the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pressure?
o: the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level
a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it
the scale that begins at absolute zero and is measured in kelvin
items.s: Pressure: the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it. The other options describe Gauge pressure, Extensive property, Thermodynamic temperature scale.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pure substance?
o: the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance
matter of fixed chemical composition that may exist in more than one phase
items.s: Pure substance: matter of fixed chemical composition that may exist in more than one phase. The other options describe Enthalpy of vaporisation, Triple point, Critical point.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings”
o: Steady flow
Flow work
Enthalpy
First law of thermodynamics
items.s: Enthalpy is the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings.

items.q: Which term is described by “the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes”?
o: Open system
Process
Quasi static process
Cycle
items.s: Process is the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes.

items.q: A gas is compressed polytropically from 250 kPa and 0.5 m3 to 600 kPa and 0.5 m3, with an index of compression of 1.2. Calculate the work input in kJ.
1 kg of air of specific heat at constant volume 0.718 kJ/kg K expands adiabatically from 600 K to 300 K. Calculate the work done in kJ.
Gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.04 kJ/kg K enters a nozzle at 550 K and leaves at 420 K with negligible inlet velocity. Calculate the exit velocity in m/s.
A gas at 290 K is compressed adiabatically through a volume ratio of 6 : 1. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.4, find the final temperature in K.
A gas at 120 kPa is compressed adiabatically to one 4th of its original volume. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.3, calculate the final pressure in kPa.
A boiler raises 4 kg/s of water from an enthalpy of 420 kJ/kg to steam of enthalpy 2900 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat added in kW.
A boiler evaporates 1.5 kg/s of water with an enthalpy rise of 2200 kJ/kg while burning 0.25 kg/s of fuel of calorific value 44000 kJ/kg. Calculate the boiler efficiency in percent.
2 kg of gas of cp = 1.1 kJ/kg K and R = 260 J/kg K is changed from 300 K and 500 kPa to 600 K and 150 kPa. Find the entropy change in kJ/K.
An air standard Diesel cycle has a compression ratio of 14 : 1 and a cut off ratio of 1.8, with gamma = 1.4. Calculate its air standard efficiency in percent.
items.s: eta = 1 - (1/r^(gamma-1))[(rc^gamma - 1)/(gamma(rc - 1))] with r = 14, rc = 1.8, gamma = 1.4 = 60.32%.

items.q: A gas turbine plant works on the air standard Brayton cycle with a pressure ratio of 6 and gamma = 1.4. Calculate the ideal cycle efficiency in percent.
A mass of 4 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 4124 J/kg K occupies 0.5 m3 at 300 K. Calculate the pressure in kPa.
The universal gas constant is 8314 J/kmol K. Find the gas constant, in J/kg K, of a gas whose molar mass is 29 kg/kmol.
A mass of 3 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 519 J/kg K occupies 1.5 m3 at a pressure of 250 kPa. Calculate its temperature in K.
Air of gas constant 287 J/kg K is at a pressure of 300 kPa and a temperature of 320 K. Calculate its density in kg/m3.
A gas has a specific heat at constant pressure of 1.2 kJ/kg K and a gas constant of 287 J/kg K. Calculate its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.
A gas has specific heats of 1.1 kJ/kg K at constant pressure and 0.82 kJ/kg K at constant volume. Calculate the ratio of specific heats.
A gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.005 kJ/kg K has a ratio of specific heats of 1.35. Find its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.
A rigid vessel of volume 1.5 m3 contains steam of specific volume 0.2 m3/kg. Calculate the mass of steam in the vessel in kg.
A quantity of 200 kJ of heat raises the temperature of a body of specific heat capacity 2.1 kJ/kg K by 10 K. Find its mass in kg.
A gas expands at a constant pressure of 100 kPa from 0.3 m3 to 2.5 m3. Calculate the work done in kJ.
2 kg of gas of specific heat at constant pressure 2.1 kJ/kg K is heated through 25 K at constant pressure. Find the heat supplied in kJ.
items.s: Q = m cp dT = 2 x 2.1 x 25 = 105 kJ.

items.q: Find the change in internal energy, in kJ, of 2 kg of gas of specific heat at constant volume 0.75 kJ/kg K when its temperature rises by 60 K.
items.s: dU = m cv dT = 2 x 0.75 x 60 = 90 kJ.

items.q: During a process a closed system absorbs heat while its internal energy rises by 150 kJ and it does 10 kJ of work. Calculate the heat absorbed in kJ.
Calculate the change in enthalpy, in kJ, of 4 kg of gas of specific heat at constant pressure 2.1 kJ/kg K when it is heated through 50 K.
items.s: dH = m cp dT = 4 x 2.1 x 50 = 420 kJ.

items.q: A mass of 0.5 kg of gas with gas constant 260 J/kg K is held at 250 kPa and 300 K. Find its volume in m3.
A sample of wet steam has a specific volume of 0.15 m3/kg. At the same pressure the saturated liquid and dry saturated vapour values are 0.0012 and 0.2 m3/kg. Calculate the dryness fraction.
Wet steam has a dryness fraction of 0.85, with hf = 640 kJ/kg and hfg = 2257 kJ/kg at its pressure. Calculate its specific enthalpy in kJ/kg.
A reversible engine works between a source at 450 K and a sink at 300 K. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
A Carnot engine receives 1000 kJ of heat from a reservoir at 500 K and rejects heat to a sink at 300 K. Calculate the work output in kJ.
An engine receives 800 kJ of heat and delivers 300 kJ of work. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.
A heat engine takes in 800 kJ of heat and produces 250 kJ of work. Find the heat rejected to the sink in kJ.
A refrigerator removes 400 kJ of heat from a cold space while consuming 75 kJ of work. Calculate its coefficient of performance.
An air standard Otto cycle operates with a compression ratio of 6 : 1 and gamma = 1.35. Calculate its air standard efficiency in percent.
3 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 287 J/kg K expands isothermally at 320 K until its volume is 3 times the original. Calculate the work done in kJ.
items.s: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) = 3 x 287 x 320 x ln 3 = 302.7 kJ.

Gas of specific heat at constant pressure 1.04 kJ/kg K enters a nozzle at 500 K and leaves at 380 K with negligible inlet velocity. Calculate the exit velocity in m/s.
A gas at 320 K is compressed adiabatically through a volume ratio of 5 : 1. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.4, find the final temperature in K.
A gas at 100 kPa is compressed adiabatically to one 2th of its original volume. Taking the ratio of specific heats as 1.4, calculate the final pressure in kPa.
A boiler raises 5 kg/s of water from an enthalpy of 400 kJ/kg to steam of enthalpy 2700 kJ/kg. Calculate the heat added in kW.

4 kg of gas of cp = 1.1 kJ/kg K and R = 260 J/kg K is changed from 300 K and 500 kPa to 600 K and 100 kPa. Find the entropy change in kJ/K.

A mass of 3 kg of an ideal gas of gas constant 287 J/kg K occupies 1.5 m3 at 280 K. Calculate the pressure in kPa.

Air of gas constant 519 J/kg K is at a pressure of 200 kPa and a temperature of 290 K. Calculate its density in kg/m3.
A gas has a specific heat at constant pressure of 1.04 kJ/kg K and a gas constant of 296 J/kg K. Calculate its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.

A gas of specific heat at constant pressure 2.1 kJ/kg K has a ratio of specific heats of 1.41. Find its specific heat at constant volume in kJ/kg K.

items.q: In this course, Enthalpy of vaporisation refers to
o: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition
the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point
the energy needed to turn unit mass of saturated liquid into dry saturated vapour
the pressure at which a liquid boils at a given temperature

items.q: In this course, Diesel cycle refers to
o: the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
the delivery pressure of a compressor divided by the pressure at its inlet
