items.q: Which statement correctly defines Specific heat at constant pressure?
o: the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the pressure is held fixed
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
items.s: Specific heat at constant pressure: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the pressure is held fixed. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Polytropic process, Specific heat at constant volume.

items.q: In this course, Closed system refers to
o: a region of fixed mass across whose edge only energy may pass
a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions
a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from
a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition
items.s: Closed system: a region of fixed mass across whose edge only energy may pass. The other options describe Cycle, Quasi static process, Property.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Temperature?
o: the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the mass of a substance contained in unit volume
the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
items.s: Temperature: the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow. The other options describe Intensive property, Specific volume, Density.

items.q: The correct meaning of First law of thermodynamics is
o: a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region
a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process
items.s: First law of thermodynamics: the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process. The other options describe Flow work, Throttling, Diffuser.

items.q: The correct meaning of Extensive property is
o: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the mass of a substance contained in unit volume
a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present
items.s: Extensive property: a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present. The other options describe Density, Intensive property, Absolute pressure.

items.q: In this course, Available energy refers to
o: the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work
the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
an ideal change during which the disorder of the substance stays constant
the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall
items.s: Available energy: the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work. The other options describe Principle of increase of entropy, Entropy, Isentropic process.

items.q: In this course, Compression ratio refers to
o: the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume
the ideal cycle of a gas turbine, with compression and expansion in steady flow
the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
items.s: Compression ratio: the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume. The other options describe Otto cycle, Cut off ratio, Brayton cycle.

items.q: The correct meaning of Carnot efficiency is
o: the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
items.s: Carnot efficiency: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures. The other options describe Thermal efficiency, Thermal reservoir, Coefficient of performance.

items.q: The correct meaning of Universal gas constant is
o: the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
a change carried out at constant temperature
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
items.s: Universal gas constant: the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state. The other options describe Equation of state, Polytropic process, Isothermal process.

items.q: The correct meaning of State is
o: a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition
everything outside the chosen region that can interact with it
the complete set of property values that fixes the condition of a working substance
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
items.s: State: the complete set of property values that fixes the condition of a working substance. The other options describe Property, Process, Surroundings.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work”
o: Irreversibility
Thermal efficiency
Thermal reservoir
Coefficient of performance
items.s: Thermal efficiency is the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work.

items.q: The correct meaning of Displacement work is
o: energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance
energy crossing a boundary because of a difference in temperature
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
items.s: Displacement work: the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary. The other options describe Sensible heat, Adiabatic wall, Heat.

items.q: Isothermal process may be defined as
o: a change carried out at constant temperature
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
items.s: Isothermal process: a change carried out at constant temperature. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Specific heat at constant volume, Adiabatic process.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region”
o: Internal energy
Flow work
Diffuser
Enthalpy
items.s: Flow work is the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region.

items.q: In this course, Air standard cycle refers to
o: the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas
the delivery pressure of a compressor divided by the pressure at its inlet
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
items.s: Air standard cycle: an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas. The other options describe Diesel cycle, Cut off ratio, Pressure ratio.

items.q: Three of these relate to Pure substances and steam. Which one does not?
o: Coefficient of performance
Saturation temperature
Saturation pressure
Pure substance
items.s: Every other option belongs to Pure substances and steam. “Coefficient of performance” belongs to Second law, not Pure substances and steam.

items.q: “a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another” is the definition of
o: Polytropic process
Ideal gas
Adiabatic process
Specific heat at constant pressure
items.s: Ideal gas is a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another.

items.q: Work may be defined as
o: energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature
energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
the energy needed to raise unit mass of a substance through one degree
items.s: Work: energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance. The other options describe Latent heat, Displacement work, Specific heat capacity.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Ideal gas.
o: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the pressure is held fixed
items.s: Ideal gas: a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another. The other options describe Specific heat at constant pressure, Equation of state, Specific heat at constant volume.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Saturation temperature.
o: a mixture of liquid droplets and vapour in equilibrium at the saturation condition
vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure
the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure
the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance
items.s: Saturation temperature: the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure. The other options describe Triple point, Wet vapour, Superheated vapour.

items.q: “a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present” is the definition of
o: Intensive property
Thermodynamic temperature scale
Density
Absolute pressure
items.s: Intensive property is a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present.

items.q: In this course, Flow work refers to
o: the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules
a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region
the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process
items.s: Flow work: the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region. The other options describe Internal energy, Diffuser, First law of thermodynamics.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Gauge pressure.
o: the scale that begins at absolute zero and is measured in kelvin
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level
the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it
items.s: Gauge pressure: the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level. The other options describe Intensive property, Pressure, Thermodynamic temperature scale.

items.q: In this course, Coefficient of performance refers to
o: an ideal change that can be reversed without leaving any trace on the surroundings
the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes
the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
items.s: Coefficient of performance: the heat moved by a refrigerating device divided by the work it consumes. The other options describe Carnot efficiency, Reversible process, Heat engine.

items.q: “the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone” is the definition of
o: Irreversibility
Coefficient of performance
Thermal efficiency
Second law of thermodynamics
items.s: Irreversibility is the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Isolated system.
o: a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition
the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them
the path of successive conditions followed by a substance as it changes
a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
items.s: Isolated system: a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it. The other options describe Property, Thermodynamics, Process.

items.q: The correct meaning of Specific heat at constant volume is
o: a gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no force on one another
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
a change carried out at constant temperature
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
items.s: Specific heat at constant volume: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed. The other options describe Isothermal process, Ideal gas, Adiabatic process.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level”
o: Thermodynamic temperature scale
Intensive property
Pressure
Gauge pressure
items.s: Gauge pressure is the value read on an instrument, measured above or below the surrounding atmospheric level.

items.q: “a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature” is the definition of
o: Coefficient of performance
Reversible process
Carnot efficiency
Thermal reservoir
items.s: Thermal reservoir is a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Thermodynamics.
o: the closed surface that separates the matter under study from everything around it
a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition
a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them
items.s: Thermodynamics: the science that treats energy, its transformations and the laws that govern them. The other options describe Property, Boundary, Isolated system.

items.q: Steady flow may be defined as
o: a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance
a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
a flow in which conditions at any fixed point do not change with time
items.s: Steady flow: a flow in which conditions at any fixed point do not change with time. The other options describe Throttling, Control volume, Diffuser.

items.q: In this course, Specific heat at constant volume refers to
o: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the pressure is held fixed
a change during which no thermal energy crosses the boundary
items.s: Specific heat at constant volume: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed. The other options describe Adiabatic process, Ratio of specific heats, Specific heat at constant pressure.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Indicator diagram.
o: energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature
the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area
energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance
a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
items.s: Indicator diagram: the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area. The other options describe Adiabatic wall, Latent heat, Work.

items.q: Control volume may be defined as
o: the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance
the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region
a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
a flow in which conditions at any fixed point do not change with time
items.s: Control volume: the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance. The other options describe Diffuser, Steady flow, Flow work.

items.q: In this course, Critical point refers to
o: the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure
the pressure at which a liquid boils at a given temperature
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure
items.s: Critical point: the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other. The other options describe Saturation pressure, Superheated vapour, Saturation temperature.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Diesel cycle.
o: the ideal cycle in which heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
an ideal cycle in which the working fluid is treated as a fixed mass of perfect gas
items.s: Diesel cycle: the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure. The other options describe Cut off ratio, Dual cycle, Air standard cycle.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present”
o: Intensive property
Temperature
Gauge pressure
Extensive property
items.s: Intensive property is a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present.

items.q: In this course, Enthalpy refers to
o: the statement that energy can be transformed but never created or destroyed in a process
the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance
a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings
items.s: Enthalpy: the sum of the internal energy of a substance and the flow work needed to place it in its surroundings. The other options describe Control volume, Throttling, First law of thermodynamics.

items.q: In this course, Equation of state refers to
o: the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed
a change carried out at constant temperature
the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air
items.s: Equation of state: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas. The other options describe Specific heat at constant volume, Ratio of specific heats, Isothermal process.

items.q: The correct meaning of Control volume is
o: a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
the energy used to push a fluid across the edge of an open region
the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance
a duct of decreasing area in which a fluid gains velocity at the expense of pressure
items.s: Control volume: the fixed region chosen for analysis of a flowing substance. The other options describe Flow work, Throttling, Nozzle.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance”
o: Latent heat
Sensible heat
Specific heat capacity
Displacement work
items.s: Sensible heat is energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance.

items.q: In this course, Heat engine refers to
o: the greatest possible fraction of heat convertible to work between two fixed temperatures
the feature of a real change that prevents it from being exactly undone
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
items.s: Heat engine: a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest. The other options describe Thermal reservoir, Irreversibility, Carnot efficiency.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Specific volume?
o: the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance
the mass of a substance contained in unit volume
the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
the scale that begins at absolute zero and is measured in kelvin
items.s: Specific volume: the volume occupied by unit mass of a substance. The other options describe Density, Absolute pressure, Thermodynamic temperature scale.

items.q: “the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules” is the definition of
o: Internal energy
First law of thermodynamics
Nozzle
Throttling
items.s: Internal energy is the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules.

items.q: “the principle that heat cannot pass from a colder body to a hotter one without work being spent” is the definition of
o: Irreversibility
Second law of thermodynamics
Coefficient of performance
Thermal efficiency
items.s: Second law of thermodynamics is the principle that heat cannot pass from a colder body to a hotter one without work being spent.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Critical point?
o: the single condition at which solid, liquid and vapour exist together in balance
vapour at a temperature above the saturation value for its pressure
the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other
the energy needed to raise unit mass of liquid from the reference condition to the saturation point
items.s: Critical point: the condition beyond which liquid and vapour cannot be distinguished from each other. The other options describe Superheated vapour, Triple point, Sensible enthalpy of liquid.

items.q: The correct meaning of Otto cycle is
o: the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
the volume at the end of constant pressure heat addition divided by the volume at its start
the ideal cycle of a gas turbine, with compression and expansion in steady flow
items.s: Otto cycle: the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume. The other options describe Cut off ratio, Diesel cycle, Brayton cycle.

items.q: The correct meaning of Temperature is
o: the value measured from a complete vacuum as its zero
a characteristic whose value does not depend on the amount of matter present
the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow
the normal force exerted by a fluid on unit area of the surface containing it
items.s: Temperature: the property that fixes the thermal level of a body and decides the direction of heat flow. The other options describe Intensive property, Pressure, Absolute pressure.

items.q: “the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air” is the definition of
o: Adiabatic process
Universal gas constant
Gas constant
Ratio of specific heats
items.s: Ratio of specific heats is the quotient of the constant pressure value by the constant volume value, about 1.4 for air.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed”
o: Universal gas constant
Molar mass
Adiabatic process
Specific heat at constant volume
items.s: Specific heat at constant volume is the energy that raises unit mass through one degree when the volume is held fixed.

items.q: In this course, Diathermic wall refers to
o: the energy needed to raise unit mass of a substance through one degree
the energy transferred when a fluid expands or is compressed against a resisting boundary
energy crossing a boundary because a force acts through a distance
a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise
items.s: Diathermic wall: a barrier that lets thermal energy pass freely so that temperatures equalise. The other options describe Displacement work, Work, Specific heat capacity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Throttling?
o: a duct of increasing area in which a fluid loses velocity and gains pressure
a duct of decreasing area in which a fluid gains velocity at the expense of pressure
the energy stored inside a substance by the motion and arrangement of its molecules
a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added
items.s: Throttling: a flow through a restriction in which pressure falls while no work is done and no heat is added. The other options describe Internal energy, Nozzle, Diffuser.

items.q: “the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure” is the definition of
o: Superheated vapour
Wet vapour
Saturation temperature
Enthalpy of vaporisation
items.s: Saturation temperature is the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil at a given pressure.

items.q: In this course, Quasi static process refers to
o: a region that exchanges neither mass nor energy with what lies outside it
a region of fixed mass across whose edge only energy may pass
a region through which both mass and energy may flow
a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions
items.s: Quasi static process: a change slow enough for the substance to pass through a series of near equilibrium conditions. The other options describe Isolated system, Open system, Closed system.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Universal gas constant.
o: the relation linking pressure, volume and temperature for a fixed mass of gas
a change that follows a path of the form pressure times volume to a fixed power equals a constant
the mass of one kilomole of a substance
the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state
items.s: Universal gas constant: the constant that applies to one kilomole of any gas in the equation of state. The other options describe Molar mass, Equation of state, Polytropic process.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Thermal reservoir.
o: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature
a device that takes heat from a hot store, converts part of it to work and rejects the rest
the fraction of the heat supplied to a cycle that appears as net work
the principle that heat cannot pass from a colder body to a hotter one without work being spent
items.s: Thermal reservoir: a body so large that taking heat from it or giving heat to it does not change its temperature. The other options describe Heat engine, Second law of thermodynamics, Thermal efficiency.

items.q: The correct meaning of Isentropic process is
o: the property that measures molecular disorder and the energy no longer available for work
an ideal change during which the disorder of the substance stays constant
the rule that the total disorder of an isolated arrangement can never fall
the part of the energy of a system that could still be converted into work
items.s: Isentropic process: an ideal change during which the disorder of the substance stays constant. The other options describe Entropy, Available energy, Principle of increase of entropy.

items.q: “a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present” is the definition of
o: Extensive property
Specific volume
Density
Absolute pressure
items.s: Extensive property is a characteristic whose value changes in proportion to the quantity of matter present.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Latent heat.
o: energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature
a barrier that allows no thermal energy to pass through it
energy absorbed or released that changes the temperature of a substance
the plot of pressure against volume from which the work of a process is read as an area
items.s: Latent heat: energy absorbed or released when a substance changes phase at constant temperature. The other options describe Adiabatic wall, Sensible heat, Indicator diagram.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from”
o: Open system
Quasi static process
Cycle
Property
items.s: Cycle is a sequence of changes that returns the substance to the condition it started from.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Compression ratio?
o: the ideal cycle of a spark ignition engine, with heat added at constant volume
the ideal cycle of a gas turbine, with compression and expansion in steady flow
the ideal cycle of a compression ignition engine, with heat added at constant pressure
the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume
items.s: Compression ratio: the total cylinder volume divided by the clearance volume. The other options describe Otto cycle, Diesel cycle, Brayton cycle.

items.q: “a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition” is the definition of
o: Closed system
Surroundings
Boundary
Property
items.s: Property is a measurable characteristic of a substance that depends only on its present condition.
